memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then he shall come out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and put it on all the horns of the altar. He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times to cleanse it and to consecrate it from the uncleanness of the Israelites." - Lev 16:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Both bloods, mixed — the bull's and the goat's. The priest's offering and the people's, applied together to the altar.

Notice what happens to the altar. It is cleansed, and then consecrated. Two movements: something removed, and something dedicated. The altar is not merely made clean; it is set apart for God's purpose.

That is always God's pattern with us. He does not forgive us and leave us idle. Cleansing is the beginning, not the end.

Paul writes to the Corinthians about the kind of lives some of them had lived, and then says: you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified (1 Cor 6:11). Washed and set apart, in the same breath.

Many believers stop at the first half. They are grateful to be forgiven but have never asked what they were forgiven for. And so they live cleansed but unused — a clean altar with no fire on it.

We are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do (Eph 2:10). Prepared in advance. There is something with your name on it.

You were not just cleaned up. You were set apart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you stopped at forgiveness without asking what God saved you for?
2. What has God set you apart to do in this season?
3. What good work has He put in front of you that you have been avoiding?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You not only cleansed me but set me apart for Your purposes. Show me the work You have prepared for me, and make me willing. Amen.
